runway.unit: bp of CAR buffer above the 10% floor

banker_read.verdict: Five sessions changed the frame, not the book: NPLs hold 32.26% on Q1, system CAR 844bp below the 10% floor on Q3 2025. BB unveiled loan-recovery mediation and an ADR track this week — a runway that repairs the tail but does not restart lending at 4.98% private credit.

tldr: The book held frozen all week — NPL 32.26%, CAR 844bp under floor.
analysis: The banking book stayed frozen and the freeze is still the story: NPLs 32.26% on Q1 2026, system CAR (Capital Adequacy Ratio) 1.56% on Q3 2025 — 844bp below the 10% floor, a cushion gone rather than thin. Neither moves until Q2 disclosure lands the court-stayed loan stock that already understates it. What changed this week was the policy scaffolding: the state floated a five-year cleanup plan, BB unveiled loan-recovery mediation and an ADR (alternative dispute resolution) track, and US Treasury officials endorsed the direction. All of it repairs the tail; none of it restarts the engine. Banks still borrow less for want of investment scope, and private credit sits at 4.98% — liquidity is not the constraint, creditworthy demand is. Dispersion stays the trade: own the private compounders, fade the SCB (State-Owned Commercial Bank) paper the resolution regime tests first.

title: T-Bonds & T-Bills
verdict: The curve caved this week — 10y −82bp, 5s10s to ~27bp.

risk: A 10y round-trip back to 10.24% if the single-print rally proves a marks artifact
Belly and long supply into FY27 re-steepening the curve

watch: Whether the 10y's 9.42% holds or mean-reverts toward the 10.24% it sat at all window

5s10s at ~27bp — the flatter slope repricing long-dated fixed-rate books
banker_read.verdict: The week repriced the whole curve, not just the front: the 10y collapsed 82bp to 9.42% and the T-bill front cut ~16bp to 9.03%, flattening 5s10s to ~27bp against a 5y anchored at 9.15%. The desk needs a second 10y mark before trusting an 82bp single-print move.

tldr: The 10y collapsed 82bp on the week to 9.42%; 5s10s flattened to ~27bp.
analysis: The week's defining move was a curve that flattened in a single print, and the size demands caution. The 10y had sat at 10.24–10.25% across the entire window; it now prints 9.42%, an 82bp collapse that drags 5s10s from ~109bp to ~27bp against a 5y anchored at 9.15%. The front corroborates the direction — the 91d cut ~16bp on the week to 9.03%, the 364d to 9.17%, the whole front sub-policy as BB's easing feeds through. Read straight, the long end finally caught the front's rally. Read sceptically, an 82bp one-day move in an illiquid long bond is as likely a marks artifact as a genuine repricing, and the round-trip back to 10.24% is real. The desk conclusion holds either way: fund term to a front that keeps falling, but do not extend duration into the 10y on a single unconfirmed print. Watch next week's auction and a second 10y mark before trusting the flatter curve.

chart_read.signal: The 10y collapsed 82bp this week to 9.42% from a static 10.24%; the 91d cut to 9.03%, the 5y held 9.15%, flattening 5s10s to ~27bp.
chart_read.context: The 10y sat at 10.24–10.25% across the whole window until this week; the front has cut at every recent auction.
chart_read.implication: ALCO: 5s10s flattens to ~27bp on one 10y print — fund term to the front, but confirm the long-end move before extending duration.

title: Iran War & Oil
verdict: Brent broke $90 and pressed to $93.69 — the shock builds.

risk: Brent above $93 stacking crude plus freight onto a $1.77bn trade gap
The fast-burning LNG subsidy compounding energy cost-push into the next CPI print

banker_read.verdict: The week's clearest external shock: Brent broke $90 and pressed to $93.69 — crude now $13.69 above the $80 FY27 assumption and still climbing. Each dollar re-widens an import bill a $1.77bn trade gap already strains and speeds a fuel-subsidy claim 43% spent in six weeks. Watch $95.

tldr: Brent broke $90 this week to $93.69, now $13.69 above the FY27 line.
analysis: Crude was the week's cleanest one-way trade, with the widest reach into the book. Brent broke $90 and pressed to $93.69, WTI $86.77 — the level that had capped it now sits below, and the move is extending rather than fading toward the $80 FY27 assumption it is now $13.69 above. The transmission into Bangladesh is direct and compounding: each dollar re-widens an import bill a $1.77bn trade gap already strains, and accelerates a fuel-subsidy claim that has burned 43% of the annual LNG provision in six weeks. It also threatens the inflation turn the MPC awaits — non-food CPI already prints 9.61%, energy cost-push not yet in the base. The desk read: crude is now the swing variable across FX, fiscal and macro at once — position for a wider import bill and a later, shallower easing path if Brent holds above $90 into next week's prints.

chart_read.context: Up from $91.52 on Thursday and now $13.69 above the $80 FY27 line — a sustained push through $90.
chart_read.implication: Treasury: each dollar on Brent re-widens the import bill and the FY27 subsidy claim — the $90 break holds, watch $95.
